To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the ground states of the Yukawa system on curved substrates are defect free for weak deformations and defect free, defect free and disclination free for stronger deformations, depending on the curvature of the substrate and on its periodicity.

(1) the curvature of the surface can be used to tune the defect density in the lattice and (2) the defect density can be tuned in a controlled manner, i.e., the defect distribution in the ground state can be tailored.

(i) the ground state of particles interacting via the Yukawa potential is defect free below a critical aspect ratio; (ii) the ground state becomes defect rich above the critical aspect ratio, and (iii) the defect distribution depends on the symmetries of the substrate.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the study of the crystalline order of two-dimensional systems on curved substrates.
the influence of weakly curved substrates on defect formation in two-dimensional systems.
the fundamental understanding of the interplay between the curvature of the substrate and the formation of defects in the crystalline order.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the curvature of the substrate is the key ingredient that determines the nature of the ground state of the system.
the defect formation on curved surfaces is a complex process that depends on the specific curvature profile of the surface.
the presence of defects in the ground state is determined by the interplay between the substrate curvature, the particle interactions, and the particle density.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the defect unbinding transitions are a consequence of the competition between the surface curvature and the long-range nature of the Yukawa interaction.
the curvature of a substrate plays an important role in the formation of crystalline order, defects, and grain boundaries.
the curvature of the substrate plays a crucial role in the formation of defects in the lattice.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the presence of defects can be used to characterize the shape of the underlying curved substrate.
, by engineering the substrate geometry and curvature, one can tune the defect structure of a crystalline lattice.
the presence of a curved surface can significantly affect the ground state structure and energetics of a two dimensional crystal.
